title: Humans Take the Stage in AI: Meta’s Phone Test Has an Unexpected New Lead
part1:
AI speaks like a human. As I imagined such a future, another actor appeared from backstage. Surprisingly, the people handling the calls were not AI, but trained contract workers.

This test was carried out on some calls through Meta’s service, Muse. The workers made the calls themselves and handled the conversations to the end. In other words, this was not a story about AI becoming more like humans. It was a story about humans entering the world behind an AI service.

This system was given the names “human concierge” and “human agent calls.” In other words, they were calls handled by a human concierge or a human representative.

Here, the cast becomes a little confusing.
part2:
With an AI service, it is easy to think that AI handles the calls, too. But in fact, human workers were standing on part of that stage. We thought AI was the lead, but it was as if humans were playing important scenes.

Of course, there is nothing wrong with humans handling calls. For difficult questions, trained people can sometimes be more helpful. The problem was that the test began without clearly explaining this to the people on the other end.

For the person receiving the call, it is important to know whether the voice on the other end belongs to AI or a human. Even in the same conversation, the sense of comfort and what people expect will change depending on who they are talking to. If a human is handling the call, it would be much clearer to say so from the start.
part3:
A vice president of Meta’s Superintelligence Labs division admitted that starting the test without properly telling people was a “mistake.” The feature in which humans handled the calls was then changed back for the time being.

At a time when there is much talk about AI taking people’s jobs, this time humans had entered the AI stage. But if the audience is not told who is backstage, they will be confused before they can enjoy the show. In phone calls in the age of AI, it is not enough to speak intelligently. It is also important to clearly say who is speaking.
in_one_line: Meta’s AI service used trained human workers for some calls without clearly telling recipients who was speaking.
